title: Dynamic Source Attribution & Schema Negotiation Proxy
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: multiple SDK versions and partner integrations send subtly different event headers and top-level fields (client_version, client_id, region_hint). This causes frequent schema-exception churn in downstream validators and opaque drops that block accurate cost and latency calculations in Console analytics.

Goal: implement a lightweight, low-latency proxy layer in the ingestion path that performs: 1) deterministic source attribution (merge client headers + token metadata + network hint), 2) adaptive schema negotiation (accept multiple known shapes and transform to canonical internal shape), 3) progressive fallback for unknown shapes with soft-accept and sampling, and 4) explicit instrumentation for why events were transformed/dropped. The proxy must preserve SLOs (median ingest latency increase <= 2ms, p95 <= 10ms) and support per-customer feature flags (enable soft-accept for some orgs).
acceptance_criteria: Proxy correctly resolves source attribution for 99.9% of test vectors (mix of SDK 0.9-1.6 and legacy partner payloads)
Unknown shape soft-accept path stores original payload in quarantine S3 and injects metadata for sampling and later repair
End-to-end ingest p95 latency increase <= 10ms measured under 75th percentile load profile
Metrics emitted for: transform_count, drop_count, quarantine_count, transform_latency_ms, attribution_confidence
Feature flag gating implemented and configurable per-organization in Console
implementation_notes: Design proxy as a sidecar microservice written in Go (low allocation, fast JSON streaming). Use ffjson / easyjson for minimal allocations.
Leverage existing schema registry table (metadata service) for known canonical mappings; add a lightweight in-memory cache with TTL 30s and version pinning per rollout.
Transformations are explicit mapping rules expressed as ordered rewrite rules (no arbitrary code execution). Rules are authored as JSON templates stored in ConfigStore and feature-flagged.
Soft-accept path: write original payload + headers + attribution vector to quarantine-bucket/<date>/<org>/<uuid>.json and create a repair_ticket in work-queue topic for offline engineers/automations.
Backpressure: when downstream validators report high error rates, enable local rate-limit token-bucket and circuit-breaker with exponential backoff and incremental sampling of soft-accepts.

Security: verify event signatures when signature header present; if verification fails, route to quarantine with 'signature_invalid' tag. Coordinate with Security for KMS access for verification keys.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): route 0.5% of traffic from internal sandbox orgs and 1 partner org. Monitor transform/dropped ratios and latency. (2 days)
Phase 1 (pilot): expand to 10% of production traffic across 5 small orgs with diverse SDK versions. Enable feature flag controls. (1 week)
Phase 2 (ramp): 50% traffic, add monitoring dashboards and automated regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets. (1 week)
Phase 3 (full): 100% traffic and deprecate fragile legacy validators after 2-week stability window. (1 week)
Rollback: immediate disable of proxy (stateless path) or switch to pass-through routing; quarantine writes are idempotent so safe to re-run repair jobs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each transform rule with golden JSON fixtures (sdk 0.9, 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, legacy partner variants)
Integration test: run proxy + validator locally against replay of 72 hours of historical events (sampled) and assert no more than 0.1% unexpected drops
Load test: synthetic load simulating 10k RPS sustained with realistic size distribution; assert p99 latency and memory usage within budget
Chaos tests: simulate slow registry cache, transient KMS failures for signature verification, and S3 write failures to ensure graceful degradation and alerting
